data.description:
# Deprecate REBAR_LLM_MODEL, add ADR and example configs

## Context / Problem
Once classes are the interface, `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is a second, ambiguous way to say the same thing —
a single scalar that cannot express a per-tier mapping. Keeping both indefinitely reintroduces the
ambiguity this epic removes. It is also load-bearing today: the production cutover's kill switch
[rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a] is documented as "point `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` back at `anthropic:...`".

## Approach
Deprecate with a migration window of one minor release. Within the window `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is still
honoured, emits a deprecation warning ONCE per process, and maps to ALL THREE classes — the
widest-compatibility reading, so an operator who set one model keeps getting exactly that model
everywhere and nothing breaks mid-window.

Deprecation (rather than keeping it as a permanent shorthand) is a deliberate operator-approved call:
there are few clients today, and it yields a single unambiguous config model.

Because the kill switch's current wording goes stale the moment this lands, rewriting it in class
terms is part of THIS ticket's contract — a kill switch that is wrong during an incident is worse than
none.

Ships example configs per provider in docs, so the easy path is documentation rather than presets
shipped in code that clients select by name.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — the deprecation warning and the map-to-all-three behaviour.
- `docs/adr/` — an ADR recording the class model and the deprecation window.
- `docs/` — example configs (Anthropic-only, Bedrock-only, mixed-provider, local+fallback).
- The cutover runbook's kill-switch entry — restated in class terms.

## Testing
Unit tier for the mapping and the warning; docs assertions for the rest.
- `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` set and no classes configured: all three classes resolve to that model.
- the deprecation warning is emitted once, not per call.
- classes configured AND `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` set: classes win, warning still emitted.
- with neither set, resolution is unchanged from today's defaults.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a test asserts `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` alone maps to all three classes
- [ ] a test asserts the deprecation warning fires exactly once per process, not per call
- [ ] a test asserts explicit class config takes precedence over `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`
- [ ] an ADR exists recording the class model, the deprecation window, and the rejected alternatives
- [ ] the cutover runbook's kill-switch entry is expressed in class terms, with no reference to
      `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` as the recovery lever
data.title: Deprecate REBAR_LLM_MODEL, add ADR and example configs
